links.label: its rule makes the comparison loop

forward_vector: I am the manifest of the pm recipe's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier: one made piece that cooks the recipe exactly as written and walks up to a blind test of its felt claim, "pm sounds still", with its chance and verdict rule set before the first trial and the page's own words named as the leak, with the fingerprint of the words it was laid against and the offers its engine measured for the text. The page is a bundle note with no frontmatter, so I am keyed by its file name, recipe-pm. I never hold the recipe's words.
grain: The page's own ## grain: six sections; one carries a piece (What you should hear). The opening, Ingredients and Where to break it carry offers only; the break's numbers are in the piece's engine and its workshop check, not in a piece of its own.

offers.section: Recipe — Cooking pm into a rhythmic phrase
offers.what: "No rotation" (:3) names a property of the group pm, and it is true of the group. What one voice shows is narrower. The Method's mirror, n → 17 − n, is the same formula as the half-turn about the seam between 8 and 9 (an identity, true of all 126 cooked loops), so on one line of hits the two can't be told apart. recipe-p2's face found the same coincidence from the other side. A possible gloss after :3: "On one line of hits a mirror in time and a half-turn about the same point are one move; pm and p2 come apart only with a second voice." Decide it with recipe-p2's Method offer, since the two are one rewrite. Read down from claim-change by the challenger.

The "Or" line (:12) is not a second choice. On a loop, the mirror n → 17 − n has two ends: the seam between 8 and 9 and the seam between 16 and 1. So "the mirror at the start" is the same mirror seen from its other end (an identity, all 126). Proposed: "The same mirror has a second end, at the start of the cycle between 16 and 1: on a loop, every mirror has two."

A note for Loudon, not a text change. Keep "or p3" (:25) until someone has heard it. What the meter reaches is the page's reason, not its comparison. Every loop recipe-p3's Method can cook has a mirror too, 10 of 10 (recipe-p3's face), so "The mirror cancels it" can't be what separates pm from p3. Whatever makes pm sound heavier than p3, if it does, is something else: p3's loops also repeat every 4 or 2 steps. The challenger disputed this offer's earlier claim-change reading ("drop 'or p3'"): a mirror found by a meter doesn't refute a felt comparison. This is what survives.

"The bilateral symmetry breaks" (:29) holds as written. Keep the hit and silence its reflection, and the 8|9 mirror is lost in 448 of 448 breaks, so one side is heavier about 8|9 every time. A precision worth a parenthesis: 16 of the 448 land on a new mirror through one of their own steps, e.g. 1 2 3 15 16 (through steps 1 and 9) and 2 4 6 11 13 (through 4 and 12). Proposed after that clause: "(about 8|9; a few breaks land on a new mirror through one of their steps)". Read down from claim-change by the challenger.

pieces.file: recipe-pm — rich — the mirror, heard blind.html
pieces.title: the mirror, heard blind · four steps
pieces.caption: **Is the mirror stiller, by ear?** Write a half in steps 1 to 8 and mirror it at 17 − n, as the Method says. On a loop that mirror has two ends, 8|9 and 16|1, so the Ingredients' "mirror at the start" is the same one. Beside it is the same half under recipe-p2's rule, played twice: the page's own "than p2". The test comes last, blind, with its rule set before the first trial: 8 trials, a fresh half each time, the order set by a coin. The rule doesn't say which loop the page expects; that is named with the score. 7 or 8 picks of one loop is a sort, each direction 3.5% by guessing. A fresh listener can take a door on step 1 straight to the test. The score says whether steps 2–3 were seen, and when they were, a 7–8 for the mirror reads "the page's direction, or the page's words". Checked in Node on the piece's own engine (workshop/rich-checks.mjs, all PASS); no agent can hear a mix, so how it sounds was not heard.

verdicts.file: recipe-pm — rich — the mirror, heard blind.html
verdicts.why: The leak is in the piece itself: step 3 states the answer ("pm sounds heavier and more settled than p2") and teaches which loop is which, so a reader who walks steps 1–3 can score 8/8 on recall. Drop that sentence, add a fresh-listener door from step 1 straight to the test, and print with the score whether steps 2–3 were seen.
